newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-London shares rocket, lira set to rejoin ERM.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-London shares rocket, lira set to rejoin ERM.

text.p: London shares took off in a surprise buying spree on Friday and the lira was a focus as Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said it would rejoin the European exchange rate mechanism in "a few hours or a few days."
The lira firmed to around 996 to the mark after starting the day at around 1000, only to fall back to around 999 by 1700 GMT after news broke that Italy had sought re-entry to Europe's currency grid.
Antonio Fazio, governor of the Bank of Italy, confirmed that the Rome government had asked for the Italian lira to be readmitted to the ERM. It crashed out of the grid in 1992.
An EU diplomat said the European Union's monetary committee will meet at one p.m. (1200 GMT) on Saturday do discuss Italy's request to rejoin the grid.

Meanwhile London's share market soared 1.64 percent to register its largest one day gain this year after a sea change in sentiment which saw worries over next Tuesday's budget and fears of rising interest rates brushed aside.

"It's incredible how quickly sentiment can change," said one senior trader. "We were expecting shares to be squeezed up because everyone was keeping positions so tight in front of the budget, but we never anticipated getting back through 4,000."
The FTSE 100 index has been unable to regain ground above 4,000 since an unexpected rise in British base rates last month.

"The futures boys have been trying to cover their short positions and we've seen some American buying on thoughts that the UK market is poised to go a lot higher after the budget," another trader said.
Traders said the reason for the change in mood was a growing optimism that Chancellor Kenneth Clarke would deliver a prudent budget next week, avoiding generous but inflationary tax giveaways.
"The Chancellor must have got the message by now," a dealer said. "His credibility is at stake."
UK gilts remained supportive and British stocks got an extra lift from Wall Street's early advance. The Dow was up 23 points as London markets closed.
French shares also surged in afternoon trading almost one percent higher to finish at a year high. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 0.98 percent at 2,255.47.
Operators cited positive trends in bonds, Wall Street, which and a recovery in the franc.

German shares ended fairly thin-volume bourse dealings 0.3 percent weaker after Wall Street closed lower overnight, with dealers saying the market was taking a breather following recent bullish trading.
"We're just seeing a small correction," said one dealer. Trade is really quiet. But things have generally been busier in the afternoons this week so the market could pick up."
The dollar settled into mid-ranges against the mark by late European trade with the market focus on the lira.

The dollar was lifted above the 1.50 level in earlier trade by comments from Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher that the current dollar rate was not in line with the economic performance of the United States.

"The Kuehbacher comments really gave it a lift above 1.50 but there's been no follow-through above 1.5040," said a Japanese bank dealer. "We're still in ranges but we've seen some excitement within these ranges."

The dollar ended unchanged against the yen after recouping some early weakness. Traders were focusing on next week's Japanese Tankan quarterly economic survey, which they expected, on balance, to be weaker and thus supportive for the dollar.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.50 yen and 1.5075 marks against 111.43 yen and 1.4980 marks late on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 64.9 points higher at 4,018.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 21.90 at 2,255.47.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 8.65 at 2,763.69. The Ibis Dax of computerised tradeing was up 3.32 points at 2768.61 by 1700 GMT.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended at $377.15 against $376.65 late on Thursday.
